It's fitting that Kucinich, whose support among Iowans has been sparse, made that statement.
Polls here show he doesn't fare well against Republican rival Rudolph Giuliani.
And, if recent conversations with his supporters are any indication, the same could be said for many of his Democratic rivals.

This state loves its politics, but even with early nominating stakes on the line, it's a lot more difficult to get a local to open up his or her wallet and commit to a specific candidate than it is to get him or her to talk about why Iowa should hold the first-in-the-nation caucuses.
"I'm not going to get involved until January," said Bob Johnson, a 64-year-old retired insurance salesman.
With 2004 fresh in his mind and a new appreciation for the value of the caucus process, Johnson is more likely to pledge his support to a candidate than he was four years ago.

Abrams became an amateur genealogist in 1972 after an aunt told her they were all named for their forebears.
The Philadelphia native wanted to know all about them.
Over the years she learned how to use library and archives holdings, how to use clues from vital records to find more.
She also learned how to read handwriting.
In 1996 she found herself on the trail of the man who adopted her daughter's birth certificate and took her away.
The woman wanted to know how many other children he had fathered.
Abrams found he had 23. Her work in that case and others led to a regular gig for the NBC's "Extra" program.
The program would pay for her hotel, Abrams, but the other expenses -- she worked pro bono -- would be hers.
She put 72,000 miles on her car and spent $12,000 of her own money.

Then the offers started pouring in from "Hard Copy," "Investigative Reports," "The Montel Williams Show," "Leeza Gibbons," "Larry King Live" and "The Maury Povich Show." She worked with the Philadelphia TV station WHYY on a documentary called "The Family History Detective." And she consulted for the show "Genealogy Roadshow." She has helped reunite a woman with her mother who had been kidnapped by a grandmother who didn't want her husband to know she'd gotten pregnant as a teenager.
She has helped trace a baby stolen by a nurse who was given to a couple who had lost a baby.
